# dtcloud_projects (Data Source)

Lists the projects on the account, and reports which one the provider is currently scoped to.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_projects" "all" {}

output "active_project" {
  value = data.dtcloud_projects.all.active_project_name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `active_project_id` (String) The project the caller's session is currently pointed at. Everything this provider creates lands in it.
- `active_project_name` (String) Name of that project.
- `active_region_id` (Number) The region the caller's session is currently pointed at.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `projects` (List of Object) The projects visible to the caller. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--projects))

<a id="nestedatt--projects"></a>
### Nested Schema for `projects`

Read-Only:

- `domain_id` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

~> **`active_project_id` is where everything lands.** Every resource this provider creates goes into
that project. Outputting it in a configuration that manages more than a handful of resources makes a
misconfigured credential obvious rather than surprising.

* **Changing the active project is not exposed.** The API has an endpoint for it, but it switches the
  caller's session rather than any infrastructure, so driving it from Terraform would silently move
  where every other call lands.
